title: A deadline can be counted two ways
when: A contract deadline comes out differently depending on how it is counted (for example business days or calendar days).
steps: Agent 07 (Transaction Coordinator) does not pick one.
It asks the authorized user, showing both dates.
why: A wrong deadline can void a contingency or breach the contract. How to count is a contract reading, and that is for the authorized user.
you_see: A question showing both calculated dates.
test: A transaction's timeline is set. The authorized user relays, as a signed setting, that the inspection deadline is October 27 counting business days or October 25 counting calendar days. (No entry reads a contract today, so the question reaches the system as the authorized user's setting.)

title: A party says a deadline was extended, but there is no amendment
when: Someone says a deadline was extended and no signed amendment is on file.
steps: Agent 07 keeps tracking the original deadline.
It tells the authorized user an extension was claimed with no amendment on file.
never: Move a deadline on someone's word.
why: Only a signed amendment changes a contract date. Tracking a claimed date could let the real one pass.
you_see: A question saying an extension was claimed with no amendment.
test: A transaction with an inspection deadline of October 25; a party claims the inspection deadline was extended, with no amendment on file.

title: A document contradicts a tracked deadline
when: A document comes in that states a different date for a milestone than the one being tracked.
steps: Agent 07 stops that milestone: it is not marked satisfied.
It raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user with both dates.
A document whose dates agree is filed normally.
never: Pick one of the two dates, or mark the milestone done.
why: Two dates for one deadline means one is wrong. Until the authorized user settles it, acting on either could miss the real one.
you_see: A legal-line alert showing the tracked date and the date in the document.
test: Two transactions track an inspection deadline of October 25. On the first, the inspection report states October 22: alert, report not logged as received. On the second, the report states October 25: filed normally, no alert.

title: Several deadlines fall on the same day
when: Two or more milestones are due on the same day.
steps: Agent 07 sends a separate warning for each milestone.
It never rolls them into one combined alert.
never: Summarize several deadlines into one alert.
why: A combined alert is easy to clear after handling only one item. One alert per deadline means each one gets attention.
test: Inspection and appraisal are both due October 20. On the daily run that day, each gets its own warnings.

title: Wire instructions come up anywhere
when: Wiring money comes up in any message or document (for example "updated wire instructions").
steps: Everything stops for that message: Agent 11 (Client Communication) catches it before it reaches the document or transaction agents.
It raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user, flagged for checking outside the system.
Nothing is handled partially.
never: Pass on, confirm or act on wire instructions in any message.
why: Wire fraud is the most common way buyers lose their down payment. Wire details are confirmed by phone with a known number, never through messages.
you_see: A legal-line alert about the wire message.
test: A party sends a settlement statement with the message "Here are the updated wire instructions for closing".

title: The inspection report arrives
steps: Agent 07 records that the report was received.
If the report includes repair requests, that part goes only to the authorized user: a legal-line alert names the repair negotiation.
never: Draft, suggest or send anything about repair negotiation.
why: Repair negotiation is advice and negotiation on the client's behalf. That is licensed work for a person.
you_see: The report logged as received; a legal-line alert about the repair negotiation.
test: An inspection report with repair requests is submitted.

title: The appraisal comes in below the contract price
when: The appraised value is lower than the contract price.
steps: Agent 07 records the fact.
It raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user: every option from here is for the authorized user.
never: Draft or suggest ways to cover the gap.
why: An appraisal gap means renegotiating, paying cash or walking away. Those are legal and financial decisions for people.
you_see: A legal-line alert saying the appraisal is below the contract price.
test: An appraisal of $430,000 against a contract price of $450,000.

title: The financing contingency date passes with no removal on file
when: The financing contingency deadline passes and no contingency removal is on file.
steps: On the daily run after the date passes, Agent 07 raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user.
It never assumes the contingency was waived.
never: Treat silence as a waived contingency.
why: Whether a contingency still protects the buyer changes who loses the deposit. That has to be confirmed, not assumed.
you_see: A legal-line alert naming the financing contingency.
test: Financing contingency due October 20; the daily clock runs October 21 with no removal on file.

title: A title exception shows up
when: The title commitment lists an exception (for example an easement).
steps: Agent 07 sends the authorized user the exception word for word in a legal-line alert.
It never says how serious it is.
never: Characterize a title exception as minor, standard or serious.
why: Judging a title exception is legal advice. The exact text goes to the authorized user and the title professionals.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the exception.
test: A title commitment with the exception "Recorded easement for a utility line along the rear lot".

title: The closing date moves on someone's word
when: Someone says the closing date has moved, but no amendment is signed.
steps: Agent 07 keeps tracking the original closing date until an amendment is signed.
never: Change the tracked closing date without a signed amendment.
why: A verbal date change is not binding. Tracking it could let the contract date pass unnoticed.
you_see: The original closing date still tracked.
test: Closing on November 20; a verbal move to November 25 is reported with no signed amendment.

title: The earnest money receipt is not confirmed by its deadline
when: The earnest money deadline passes with no receipt on file.
steps: On the daily run after the deadline, Agent 07 raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user.
Money milestones never get the benefit of the doubt.
why: A missing deposit can be a default under the contract, or a sign of fraud. The authorized user needs to know at once.
you_see: A legal-line alert naming the earnest money.
test: Earnest money due October 20; the daily clock runs October 21 with no receipt on file.

title: The possession terms are unclear
when: The contract's possession terms can be read more than one way.
steps: Agent 07 asks the authorized user, quoting the exact clause.
It never fills in what the parties probably meant.
why: When the buyer gets the keys matters to both families. Reading intent into a clause is legal interpretation.
you_see: A question quoting the possession clause.
test: The authorized user relays, as a signed setting, the clause "Possession at closing or as agreed".
